options.text: An append to the main queue that the next command folds by id is acceptable, because the move is idempotent; a failure after a complete copy may remove the copied files, per file only after that file's content is present in the main store. A failed move exits 1, loses nothing and duplicates nothing, every entry the worktree held stays readable from the worktree or the main checkout, and the next command completes the move with each id once.
A failure-atomic move: a failed move leaves the main queue untouched and removes nothing the worktree holds.

options.text: Compare bytes. Identical content already in the main store means the held file is removed and nothing is copied twice; different content under the same name in the main store means the held content is kept under a fresh name in the main store (never overwritten, never lost) before the held file is removed. Because an outbox bundle is the feedback a session flushed for submission, the guarantee does not depend on whether a file is derived.
A Define amendment: outbox bundles, as derived flushes of pending titles, fall outside the per-file guarantee, and store.js:198 stays as it is.

decisions.question: (FBS-231 round 6, run 2 of the Define, on top of decision 84) The round 6 sweep pins every concurrent path on the held queue and the main outbox; three paths its Define named under further defects lose ask records in the main checkout's own state.json: two Stop hooks in one checkout at once (src/cli/feedback.js:2300 reads the ledger, :2340 rewrites it whole, so the later write drops the earlier record), a move's whole-file rewrite of the main state.json dropping an ask record the main checkout's Stop hook wrote between the move's read and its write (src/feedback/store.js:186, :193), and a state.json read while another command is mid-write (src/feedback/store.js:184 parses it as {} and the move rewrites state.json without the main checkout's records; readAskLedger at :431 throws on it and the Stop hook fails). How does round 6 serialise the commands that write the main checkout's feedback store, and what does a command do that finds the store busy?

options.text: The stage-keeper's ruling. The main checkout's feedback store is a shared resource, so every writer of it takes one store-wide lock for its whole read-modify-write span: the held-queue move, rcf feedback add, the Stop hook's ledger write, the SessionEnd bundle write and the submit bundle write. The lock is a file in the main store, created with exclusive create, holding the pid, the hostname and the start time; it is stale, and may be broken by exclusive re-create, when the holder pid is not alive on this host or it is older than 60 seconds. The move, finding the lock held by a live holder, skips (as ruled before). Every other writer waits for the lock, polling briefly, for up to 10 seconds; if it still cannot take it, it exits 1 naming the lock holder and the main checkout and writes nothing (nothing half-done). state.json and entries.jsonl are replaced atomically (a temp file in the same directory, then rename), so no reader ever sees a half-written file; bundles are created with exclusive create, with a unique suffix only on collision.

Serialise the move only and leave the other writers as they are: rcf feedback add, the Stop hook, the SessionEnd hook and submit keep an unlocked read-modify-write, so the three paths above stay open and are batched as P3.

decisions.question: (FBS-231 round 6, run 3 of the Define, on top of decisions 84 and 85) The round 6 builder escalated without code: under decision 85 every writer of the main checkout's store waits on the store-wide lock, so the run 1 tests that held a worktree move inside its locked span and then awaited a main checkout writer before letting the move go would hold that writer for its whole 10 second wait (test/feedback/worktree-held-queue-concurrent.test.js, the add, SessionEnd and submit paths), and one of them could not be told apart from the writers-wait-runs-out test of run 2. When is a held lock stale, and how do the tests hold a move while a writer waits on it?

options.text: The stage-keeper's ruling, refining decision 85's stale rule. The lock holder refreshes the lock (rewrites its timestamp) at least every 5 seconds while it works; a lock is stale, and may be broken by exclusive re-create, only when its holder pid is not alive on this host or it has not been refreshed for 60 seconds. A running move is therefore never broken. The run 1 tests that hold a move while a main checkout writer runs start the writer while the move is held, wait until the writer has run to its end or found the store busy, then let the move go, then await the writer. AC-16103-4's stale sentence says not refreshed for 60 seconds in place of started more than 60 seconds earlier.
Keep decision 85's stale rule (older than 60 seconds by its start time): a move still running after 60 seconds may be broken by a waiting writer, and only the test order changes.

decisions.question: (FBS-231 round 7 Define, on top of decisions 84 to 86) The round 6 gate returned FINDINGS at d284cf91 with AC-16103-4 partial: Codex R6-BH1 (the stale-lock break can leave two holders; the reviewer's probe g9 L9, three Stop hooks breaking one dead holder's lock, lost two of three ask records), R6-BH2 (appendEntry and appendState still append in place, so a reader can meet a half-written line, against decision 85), R6-BH3 (the CHANGELOG line is untrue while those stand) and R6-BE1 (AC-16103-4 claims stand while it is partial); the reviewer's R6-1 (the same as R6-BH1) and R6-2 (a busy store after submit has filed an issue exits 1 saying it wrote nothing, so the entry stays pending and the next submit files it twice); the reviewer's P3 note that an opted-out Stop hook waits 10 seconds and exits 1 while the store is busy; and Codex asking that a malformed lock name a pid. The owner questions, quoted: 'Fix R6-1, R6-2 and R6-BH2 now or batch them as P3? Should an opted-out Stop hook skip the lock? Should a malformed lock name a pid (Codex)?'

options.text: The stage-keeper's ruling: fix them in round 7. (1) Breaking a stale lock is safe for any number of concurrent breakers: exactly one breaker ends up holding the lock and every other command either waits as a writer or skips as a move; a breaker never deletes a lock it did not judge, and a fresh holder's lock is never removed. (2) Every write to entries.jsonl and state.json (appendEntry and appendState included) replaces the whole file atomically (a temp file in the same directory, then rename), as decision 85 already says, so no reader ever sees a partial line or document. (3) After an external side effect (submit has filed the issue), the write that records it is never abandoned on a busy store: it waits for the lock up to the stale window plus a margin (65 seconds of Date, injectable for tests as RCF_FEEDBACK_LOCK_WAIT_MS is), so a hung holder is broken as stale and the record lands; if it still cannot write, it exits 1 naming the filed issue's URL and the entry id and never says it wrote nothing, and the next submit does not file that entry again (it reads a record of the filing it can trust). (4) A Stop hook that has opted out and writes nothing takes no lock and never waits. (5) A lock file that cannot be parsed is reported by path and age, and is judged stale by its mtime as the build already does.
Batch R6-1, R6-2 and R6-BH2 as P3: release round 6 as it stands and note them for a later round.
